concepts.def: Increasing proportion of population living in cities; 56% globally in 2020, projected 68% by 2050.
Urban area with 10 million+ inhabitants; over 33 worldwide; mostly in NICs (Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai, Sao Paulo).
Push: rural poverty, lack of jobs, drought; pull: employment, education, healthcare, services; drives rural-urban migration.
Brazilian megacity (13 million) with extreme inequality; wealthy beachside districts (Ipanema) and favelas like Rocinha.
Rio scheme upgrading favelas: paved roads, sewers, schools; improved conditions for 250,000 people.
Africa's largest city (15 million); rapid growth, traffic gridlock; Eko Atlantic land-reclamation project responds.

Changing Urban Areas — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Changing Urban Areas brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Changing Urban Areas.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
